title: Secrets and environment management: per-environment variables set in the browser, delivered to runs, never logged
description:
Filed by architect-16a01670 from parent task-e7a3d643bde34da7b27495dbda745739 (epic breakdown, human-directed 2026-09-04; owner chose Stage 1 + Stage 2 scope).

VISION Stage 2 'secrets and environment management'. Re-measured 2026-09-04: seats and the verifier receive an allowlisted env built by the wrapper (apps/daemon/src/orchestrator/agent-spawn-environment.ts, verifier-process-runner.ts); there is no per-project / per-environment variable store and no UI; the scaffold profile needs DATABASE_URL, session secrets and third-party keys per environment.

FEATURE: an ENVIRONMENTS model per project: environments (verify, preview, production) x variables. The approved contract's deployment requirements enumerate the REQUIRED variable names (the compiler emits them; a goal shows which are unset). `environment.set_variable {environment, name, value}` and `environment.unset_variable` are operator-only and MCP-excluded; values are stored encrypted at rest in the project store (key derived from the daemon credential, or Windows DPAPI - architect decides; a copied store without the key must be useless) and NEVER appear in events, receipts, logs, reads or refusals - reads return {name, isSet, sha256 fingerprint, updatedAt}. Delivery: the verifier, preview and deploy process spawns receive the environment's variables merged under the wrapper allowlist; a `.env.example` listing names only is generated into the repository through the lander.

UI: Environments screen (per environment: required vs set, set/unset dialogs, fingerprint, last update); the goal shows 'N required variables unset for preview' with a link. Refusals: ENV_NAME_INVALID, ENV_VALUE_TOO_LARGE, ENV_ENVIRONMENT_UNKNOWN, ENV_STORE_KEY_UNAVAILABLE.

This is a feature row (Stage 2 capability); it adds no trust boundary and changes none.
definitionOfDone: `environment.set_variable` and `environment.unset_variable` published operator-only, MCP-excluded, with the full roster backfill and bidirectional roster tests; ENV_NAME_INVALID, ENV_VALUE_TOO_LARGE, ENV_ENVIRONMENT_UNKNOWN, ENV_STORE_KEY_UNAVAILABLE asserted with code + layer.

Canary test: set a value `MOE_CANARY_<random>`; grep the store file bytes, the event stream, every read response, the wrapper log and every receipt - 0 occurrences of the plaintext while the fingerprint is present; the variable reaches a spawned verifier process (the test asserts the child saw it).
Encrypted at rest proven: a copied store opened without the key answers ENV_STORE_KEY_UNAVAILABLE and yields no plaintext (asserted on bytes).
Environments screen against a REAL daemon (Playwright): required-vs-set table, set/unset round trip, fingerprint changes on update; the goal card shows the unset count; count line quoted.

`.env.example` (names only) generated and landed; runbook documents the model; gates quoted with count lines: `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test`, `pnpm --filter @moe/control-room test`, `pnpm typecheck`, `pnpm test`.

A new daemon read/command follows the 8-touchpoint + .js bridge pattern (memory ui-connect-everything-built-2026-09-02).

implementationPlan.note:
ADVERSARIAL PASS. All four questions answered on the delivered tree. Nothing "not covered" except the one item already filed in comment-262254a4. (Keeping this under the 5000-char cap: my first three notes were silently truncated at exactly 5000 and their tails are restated in comment-262254a4 and comment-a7e4fbb7.)

**(a) THE ALLOWLIST WAS NOT WIDENED — asserted, then DRILLED, on both of its two independent mechanisms.**
Code: `agentEnvironment()` builds from `source` through the closed roster (`RUNTIME_ENVIRONMENT_KEYS` :14, `PROVIDER_ENVIRONMENT_PREFIXES` :28), then applies `delivered` LAST at `:105` to the finished object — never folded into `source`. The `:55-58` comment states the converse too: folding it in "would drop every arbitrary operator name and the only way to make one arrive would be to widen the roster."
Test, in `environment-composed-canary.test.ts`: an unrostered host name (`ROLLUP_HOST_ONLY`) is ABSENT from the child; a `MOE_`-prefixed host name (`MOE_ROLLUP_HOST_ONLY`) is ABSENT; and a DELIVERED `MOE_`-prefixed name DOES arrive. The third is what makes the first two a claim about the source loop rather than about the string "MOE_".
Drill D3 bypassed the roster check at `:67`: the host value reached the child and the arm went RED (`expected 'bf7ca9d3…' to be 'ABSENT'`). **D3 did NOT red the `moeHost` arm** — which is the proof that the roster test and the `MOE_` scrub are two lines guarding two hazards, not one guard asserted twice. Restored, `git diff` empty, sha256 equal to an out-of-tree backup.

**(b) THE COPIED STORE — the plan calls these "the adjacent case nobody owns". THEY ARE OWNED, by child 1, and better than the plan asked.** Correcting this rather than writing a duplicate. `environment-at-rest.test.ts`:
- STALE / ROTATED credential: `:123` "answers ENV_STORE_KEY_UNAVAILABLE when the credential is present but WRONG" (`OTHER_CREDENTIAL`), plus `:143` at the cipher layer — the sealed bytes taken straight out of the copy "FAIL AUTHENTICATION under a wrong credential rather than yielding garbage", reason `AUTHENTICATION_FAILED`.
- PRESENT BUT UNREADABLE: `:108`, EACCES-shaped source. And the arm nobody asked for: the thrown error names a credential PATH, so it asserts the refusal relays neither `EACCES`, nor `.moe/credential`, nor the value — a leak of WHERE the key lives, not of the key.
- EMPTY credential (`:103`, "which is how an unset env var arrives") and NO credential (`:98`).
- The two controls that stop all of the above being vacuous: `:89` the INTACT copy reads correctly with the right key, and `:159` the sealed bytes OPEN under the right credential. Without them a refusal could equally mean the copy is corrupt.
NOT COVERED, and I am not filing it: key ROTATION as a feature (re-sealing under a new credential). Out of scope by the row's FEATURES ONLY rail and by the parent's "no new trust boundary" framing.

**(c) DELIVERY IS NOT A HARD DEPENDENCY — confirmed by a committed arm, not by reading.** Second test in `environment-composed-canary.test.ts`: on a store with nothing set, `launchDelivery(config, "CODING_SEAT")` is `undefined` (withheld BY TYPE, before the store is touched — `WithheldDelivery`'s `Record<string, never>` makes `delivered["X"] = v` uncompilable), `launchDelivery(config, "VERIFIER")` is `undefined`, and `agentEnvironment(source)` vs `agentEnvironment(source, launchDelivery(...))` are equal as SORTED ENTRIES. Compared as entries deliberately, not with `toBe`: `deliverEnvironment` returns its argument BY REFERENCE when there is nothing to deliver (`:159`), so an identity check would pass while proving nothing about the bytes a child sees. `environment-delivery-canary.test.ts:222` carries the same property from the other side.

**(d) `.env.example` — I RAN THE REAL GENERATOR AND READ THE ACTUAL BYTES.** `generateControlledProfile` with `["STRIPE_SECRET_KEY","SESSION_SECRET","DATABASE_URL"]` emits two sections, and the distinction matters because a QA grading "names only" against the whole file would mis-flag the first:
```
# These are PLACEHOLDERS, not credentials.
POSTGRES_USER=app / POSTGRES_PASSWORD=CHANGE_ME / POSTGRES_DB=app
DATABASE_URL=postgres://app:CHANGE_ME@localhost:5432/app / PORT=3000

# Required by the product contract. NAMES ONLY: no value is written here, because this file is
# committed and pushed. Supply each one in .env; none has a default and none has a placeholder.
SESSION_SECRET=
```

planningNotes.risks: BIGGEST RISK — a plaintext value on a surface no child owns. Each child greps its own surfaces; the Playwright trace, the daemon log and the LANDED .env.example sit between them, and a browser trace records typed input in the one feature where an operator types a secret. Delivery merges variables into a closed roster that exists so a child sees what it needs and nothing else; a merge that hands over `process.env` plus extras destroys it and nothing fails visibly.
